Definition: Does the government maintain a separate cadastral register?
Comments: No credible evidence found for separate digital cadastral register.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original 'No' claim was unsupported and appears wrong: Burundi's Direction des Titres Fonciers et du Cadastre National (DTFCN) launched a World Bank-funded electronic records system (EDRMS) in June 2025 under the $92m PAFEN Digital Foundations Project, and a 2025-2026 national budget law now mandates digitisation of land titles (deadline extended through 2026), alongside a recently established National Centre for Geospatial Information Management. No evidence of a fully operational nationwide digital cadastral database was found, so this is 'Under development' (recalculated to 3), not 'No'.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: No credible evidence found after searching population register, national population register digital, civil register of persons, World Bank ID4D, UN CRVS, APAI-CRVS reports confirming no electronic database.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The original 'no credible evidence' finding is contradicted by UNSD's 2025 Demographic Yearbook metadata for Burundi, which confirms population estimates derive partly from a 'registre permanent de population' (permanent population register), i.e. one already exists, likely commune-level and largely paper-based historically. Separately, in May 2026 the Ministry of the Interior unveiled a World Bank-funded (PAFEN) digital civil-registration/biometric-ID platform, technically near-complete but not yet operational pending a governing decree. Recalculated from 1 (No) to 3 (Under development): a register exists and digitisation is well advanced but not yet confirmed as deployed.
